title: Close on a choice between two readings
statement: End a literature lesson's closing questions on a choice between two defensible readings that learners must justify, since a question naming the reading it wants asks only for description.
detail: A Grade 9 unit's knowledge base sets its closing questions as mimicry, then application to the extract, then an 'X or Y?' evaluation (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 140). Its quality pass flagged one lesson's question, which asked how the text presents a character as defiant and dutiful, as descriptive, not 'X or Y', and proposed asking whether she is presented as defiant or loyal (line 147). The lesson design specification's evaluation example asks learners to choose between two readings of a character and justify the view (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 192).
against: The flagged question was left unchanged (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 147); the specification's top-stage learning question asks 'to what extent' rather than offering two readings (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 135); and another record, drawn from Grade 3 reviews, bans any question answered by a two-way pick.
